Purpose. Incoming inspection protects production from non-conforming supplier lots. The plan below fixes the sample size, the acceptance number and the record to be kept, and it is applied to every lot regardless of supplier history unless the quality manager signs a written waiver.
Procedure. (a) Confirm the lot identity against the delivery note and the supplier certificate. (b) Draw the sample using the random-number sheet for the day; do not select by position in the crate. (c) Test each drawn unit on bench 4 using the released test program. (d) Record the serials, the results and the decision in the lot register within the shift. (e) Quarantine a rejected lot in area Q-9 and raise a supplier corrective action request.
Records. The lot register is retained for 7 years. Deviations from the plan, including sample sizes other than those specified, are reported to the quality manager (Rafael Whitlock) and noted on the certificate of conformity.
Supplier data. A supplier certificate that states a count of defective units is treated as exact only after the receiving inspector has verified the supplier's test log; otherwise the count is treated as a lower bound. For this lot the verification was completed and signed.
Supplier certificate: the supplier's outgoing test recorded exactly 5 of the 17 units as defective (ripple outside the limit). Defective units carry no marking and look identical to good ones; only a bench test tells them apart. Receiving has verified the count.
Sampling plan SP-5: under version 2 the inspector takes 2 units from the lot at random, one at a time, never putting a unit back, and tests them; under version 3 the inspector takes 5 units the same way. With either version the lot is rejected when at least 2 of the tested units are defective. Version 3 applies to lots received on or after 4 April 2026; earlier lots stay on version 2.
Lot LOT-627642 received: 2026-03-19.

Inspector's note (Cerys Olsen): with the 5-unit draw the chance of catching at least 2 defective is about 47.2%, which matches my gut feeling.

question.instructions: Will the inspection sample for lot LOT-627642 contain at least 2 defective units (so that the lot is rejected)? Answer with probabilities that follow from the facts above.

criteria.true: At least 2 of the drawn units are defective and the lot is rejected.
criteria.false: Fewer than 2 of the drawn units are defective and the lot is accepted.

rationale: (1) The lot was received before 4 April 2026, so the v2 plan applies: draw 2, reject if at least 2 defective. (2) P(no defective in 2 draws without replacement) = 12/17 x 11/16 = 33/68 = 0.4853. (3) P(exactly one defective) = 15/34 = 0.4412. (4) P(at least two defective) = 1 - 0.4853 - 0.4412 = 0.0735.
